lines.text: Fold paper in half ten times. Open each fold to a right angle.
Real paper jams fast, so we fold it in code.
One fold makes two segments. Two folds make four. Every fold doubles them.
Ten folds make one thousand and twenty four, and the paper opens into a dragon.
lines.caption: Ten folds make 1,024, and the paper opens into a dragon.

lines.text: It never crosses itself, and four copies fit around one point without crossing.
NASA physicists found it in the sixties: the Heighway dragon.
lines.caption: NASA physicists found it in the 1960s: the Heighway dragon.

lines.text: How many folds can you manage with real paper?

post.title: Fold a strip 10 times and a dragon appears
post.description: Fold a strip in half 10 times (simulated: real paper jams long before), open every crease to 90°, and you get the Heighway dragon: 1,024 segments that never cross. Narrated with an AI voice. Animation made with code.
post.pinned_comment: How many times could you fold real paper? Try it and tell us.
